## Function Launch Args

The argv of a claude session and the MCP config file it is given.

Behaviour: Declares in claude/args.go: `type Launch struct { Bin string; Dir string; SessionID string; Resume bool; BudgetUSD float64; Model string; MCPConfigPath string; Extra []string }`, `func Args(l Launch) []string`, `func Env(l Launch) []string`, `func MCPConfigJSON(url, token string) []byte` and `func WriteMCPConfig(dir, project, url, token string) (string, error)`. Env returns the environment entries added to the child process, always exactly []string{"CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_AUTO_MEMORY=1"} whatever the Launch holds (auto-memory is off in every phase session; it is not a configuration). Args returns, in this order: "-p", "--input-format", "stream-json", "--output-format", "stream-json", "--verbose", "--include-hook-events", "--permission-prompt-tool", "stdio", "--dangerously-skip-permissions", then "--resume", SessionID when Resume else "--session-id", SessionID; then "--max-budget-usd", strconv.FormatFloat(BudgetUSD, 'f', -1, 64) only when BudgetUSD > 0; then "--model", Model only when Model != ""; then "--mcp-config", MCPConfigPath only when it is not ""; then every Extra verbatim. Bin and Dir are not in the argv. MCPConfigJSON is the json.Marshal of {"mcpServers":{"morphd":{"type":"http","url":<url>,"headers":{"Authorization":"Bearer " + token}}}} (struct fields in that order) followed by "\n". WriteMCPConfig writes it to filepath.Join(dir, project + "-mcp.json") with mode 0o600 (dir created 0o700 when missing; an existing file is overwritten and left with mode 0o600, an os.Chmod after the write) and returns that path; a write error → ("", an error beginning "claude: mcp config: ").

Steps:
- produces: argv

Examples (the tests must prove each one):
1. given Launch{Bin: "claude", Dir: "/home/morph/projects/demo", SessionID: "11111111-2222-3333-4444-555555555555", BudgetUSD: 30, MCPConfigPath: "/tmp/demo-mcp.json"}; when Args; then exactly ["-p", "--input-format", "stream-json", "--output-format", "stream-json", "--verbose", "--include-hook-events", "--permission-prompt-tool", "stdio", "--dangerously-skip-permissions", "--session-id", "11111111-2222-3333-4444-555555555555", "--max-budget-usd", "30", "--mcp-config", "/tmp/demo-mcp.json"]
2. given Launch{SessionID: "s-2", Resume: true, BudgetUSD: 12.5, Model: "opus", MCPConfigPath: "/x/p-mcp.json", Extra: []string{"--effort", "high"}}; when Args; then the first ten entries as in example 1, then "--resume", "s-2", "--max-budget-usd", "12.5", "--model", "opus", "--mcp-config", "/x/p-mcp.json", "--effort", "high"
3. given Launch{SessionID: "s-3"} (no budget, no model, no config, no extra); when Args; then exactly the first ten entries then "--session-id", "s-3" — 12 entries
4. given the Launch of example 1; then Launch{} (every field zero); then the Launch of example 2 with Extra []string{"--effort", "high"}; when Env; then each exactly []string{"CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_AUTO_MEMORY=1"} — one entry, never more, never affected by Extra
5. given url "http://127.0.0.1:7080/mcp/demo/session", token "tok-1"; when MCPConfigJSON; then exactly {"mcpServers":{"morphd":{"type":"http","url":"http://127.0.0.1:7080/mcp/demo/session","headers":{"Authorization":"Bearer tok-1"}}}} + "\n"
6. given dir := filepath.Join(t.TempDir(), "mcp") (missing), project "demo", url "http://127.0.0.1:7181/mcp/demo/session", token "tok-2"; when WriteMCPConfig; then path == filepath.Join(dir, "demo-mcp.json"), error nil; the file holds MCPConfigJSON(url, token); its mode & 0o777 is 0o600; the directory mode & 0o777 is 0o700
7. given dir := testhelp.WriteFile(t, "f", "x") (a regular file as dir); when WriteMCPConfig; then ("", an error beginning "claude: mcp config: ")

## Component requirements / guardrails

Requirements:
- Claude Behind An Interface: The claude CLI is reached only through claude.Process (stdin lines in, stdout lines out, an exit status); the daemon's tests use claude.Fake fed with lines from tests/fixtures/stream/probe.jsonl, never a real claude.
- Bearer Token On Every Route: Every HTTP route but GET /healthz and the MCP endpoints requires Authorization: Bearer <MORPHD_TOKEN>; /mcp and /mcp/{project} require the same token; /mcp/{project}/session requires that project's current session token. morphd listens on 127.0.0.1 only; TLS and the public name are Caddy's.
- The Session Reports Only Itself: A VPS session can call phase_done, wait_operator and milestone only through its own endpoint /mcp/{project}/session with the token morphd minted for that spawn; the token changes on every spawn, so a past session or another project cannot report.

Guardrails:
- Injected Clock And Ids: No package but cmd/morphd reads the clock or a random source: time comes in as a `now` argument or an injected Now func() time.Time, ids from an injected NewID func() string; time.Now, math/rand and crypto/rand appear only in cmd/morphd. Timers are the daemon's Tick, driven by main's ticker.
- No Network In Tests: Tests never open a listener or dial: HTTP is tested with httptest.NewRecorder and httptest.NewRequest, Telegram and GitHub through an injected Do, the MCP server over in-memory transports; a test writes files only under t.TempDir(); no test runs claude or reaches github.com or api.telegram.org.
- No Shell Outside Runner: os/exec is imported only by package runner (git, morph) and package claude (the claude process); every other package runs commands through runner.Runner and tests script them with runner.Fake.
- Secrets Never Logged: The API token, the session tokens, the GitHub token and the Telegram token never appear in a response body, a log line, a milestone, an error text or the argv of a spawned process; secrets live in files of mode 0600 under the state directory; the git credentials reach git through a credential store file, never through a URL or an argument.

Write the files: `claude/args.go`.

Go 1.22, the standard library only (go.mod requires nothing; the build runs with GOPROXY=off). gofmt-formatted (gofmt -l prints nothing) and go vet clean. A file's package is its directory's base name; exported names in MixedCaps; a package imports another of the module by the module path of go.mod + "/" + its directory. Tests are `func TestXxx(t *testing.T)` in the package's own `_test.go` files, table tests allowed; compare with `testhelp.Equal(t, what, got, want)` of the module's `internal/testhelp`, never your own helper; no t.Skip, no network, no clock, no goroutine left running.

## Function Repo Access

Parse a GitHub repository URL, build the credential forms and check that a token reaches the repo with push access.

Behaviour: Declares in github/access.go: `type Access struct { Checked bool `json:"checked"`; Reachable bool `json:"reachable"`; Push bool `json:"push"`; Reason string `json:"reason"`; CheckedAt time.Time `json:"checked_at"` }`, `func Parse(repoURL string) (owner, repo string, err error)`, `func CredentialLine(token string) string`, and `func Check(ctx context.Context, do func(*http.Request) (*http.Response, error), token, repoURL string, now time.Time) Access`. Parse accepts "https://github.com/<owner>/<repo>", the same with a ".git" suffix or a trailing "/", and "git@github.com:<owner>/<repo>.git"; owner and repo are non-empty and hold no "/"; anything else → ("", "", error "github: not a github repository url: " + repoURL). CredentialLine = "https://x-access-token:" + token + "@github.com\n". Check: token "" → Access{Checked: true, Reason: "no token", CheckedAt: now}; Parse fails → {Checked: true, Reason: that error's text, CheckedAt: now}; a nil do → {Checked: true, Reason: "network: no Do", CheckedAt: now} (never a panic); else GET https://api.github.com/repos/<owner>/<repo> with headers Authorization "Bearer " + token, Accept "application/vnd.github+json", User-Agent "morphd"; the body is read and closed; by status: 200 → Reachable true, Push = permissions.push of the JSON body (false when absent), Reason ""; 401 → Reason "401 bad credentials"; 403 → "403 forbidden"; 404 → "404 not found or no access"; any other → "<status> unexpected"; Do error → Reason "network: " + err.Error() with the token replaced by "***". Checked is always true, CheckedAt = now.

Steps:
- produces: Access

Examples (the tests must prove each one):
1. given "https://github.com/VasyaLutiy/MorphStudio"; "https://github.com/VasyaLutiy/MorphStudio.git"; "https://github.com/o/r/"; "git@github.com:o/r.git"; when Parse; then ("VasyaLutiy", "MorphStudio", nil); the same; ("o", "r", nil); ("o", "r", nil)
2. given "https://gitlab.com/o/r"; "https://github.com/o"; "github.com/o/r"; ""; when Parse; then each error "github: not a github repository url: " + the input
3. given token "ghp_abc"; when CredentialLine; then exactly "https://x-access-token:ghp_abc@github.com\n"
4. given do := a recorder answering 200 with body {"full_name":"o/r","permissions":{"admin":false,"push":true,"pull":true}}; Check(ctx, do, "ghp_abc", "https://github.com/o/r", 2026-10-08T15:00:00Z); when Check; then Access{Checked: true, Reachable: true, Push: true, Reason: "", CheckedAt: 15:00:00Z}; the request: GET https://api.github.com/repos/o/r, Authorization "Bearer ghp_abc", Accept "application/vnd.github+json", User-Agent "morphd"
5. given do answering 200 with body {"permissions":{"push":false}}; then {"full_name":"o/r"} (no permissions); when Check; then Reachable true, Push false (both)
6. given do answering 401; 403; 404; 500 (any body); when Check; then Reachable false, Push false, Reasons "401 bad credentials", "403 forbidden", "404 not found or no access", "500 unexpected"
7. given Check(ctx, do, "", "https://github.com/o/r", now); Check(ctx, do, "t", "https://gitlab.com/o/r", now); when Check; then {Checked true, Reason "no token"} and do not called; {Checked true, Reason "github: not a github repository url: https://gitlab.com/o/r"} and do not called
8. given do returning errors.New("Get \"https://api.github.com/repos/o/r\": dial tcp: refused ghp_abc"); when Check(ctx, do, "ghp_abc", "https://github.com/o/r", now); then Reason exactly "network: Get \"https://api.github.com/repos/o/r\": dial tcp: refused ***"

## Function Process

A running claude process with line-delimited stdin and stdout, its exit status, and the Fake.

Behaviour: Declares in claude/process.go: `type ExitStatus struct { Code int; Stderr string }`, `type Process interface { Write(line []byte) error; Lines() <-chan []byte; Exit() <-chan ExitStatus; Stop() error; Kill() error; PID() int }`, `var ErrExited = errors.New("claude: process exited")`, `func Start(ctx context.Context, bin string, args []string, dir string, env []string) (Process, error)` and the fake: `type Fake struct` (unexported fields), `func NewFake() *Fake`, `func (f *Fake) Emit(line []byte)`, `func (f *Fake) Written() [][]byte`, `func (f *Fake) Finish(code int)`, `func (f *Fake) Killed() bool`, and *Fake implements Process (PID 4242). Start runs exec.CommandContext(ctx, bin, args...) with Dir = dir, Env = os.Environ() + env, a stdin pipe, a stdout pipe read by a goroutine with a bufio.Scanner whose buffer allows lines up to 16 MiB, each line (without the newline, empty lines skipped) sent on Lines(); stderr collected (the last 4096 bytes kept). A start failure → (nil, an error beginning "claude: start "). When the process exits: Lines() is closed, then one ExitStatus{Code: the exit code, or -1 when killed by a signal, Stderr: the kept bytes} is sent on Exit() (a buffered channel of 1) and Exit() closed. Write appends nothing (the caller gives the newline) and writes under a mutex; after the exit it returns ErrExited. Stop closes stdin (the CLI exits on EOF). The process leads its own group: cmd.SysProcAttr = &syscall.SysProcAttr{Setpgid: true}; Kill sends SIGKILL to the whole group (syscall.Kill(-pid, syscall.SIGKILL)) and cmd.Cancel (the context's end) does the same — /bin/sh (dash) does not exec a script's last command, and a child left alive holds the stdout and stderr pipes, so Lines() would never close. PID is the OS pid. Fake: Lines() is a buffered channel (1024 lines), so Emit never blocks before a reader; Emit delivers a line on Lines(); Written returns a copy of every Write in order; Finish(code) closes Lines() and delivers ExitStatus{Code: code}; Write after Finish → ErrExited; Kill sets Killed and, if not finished, Finish(-1); Stop finishes with 0 if not finished; after the finish, Emit is dropped and Finish, Stop, Kill deliver nothing more (never a panic). Every Fake method is safe for concurrent use.

Steps:
- produces: ExitStatus

Examples (the tests must prove each one):
1. given bin := a script written under t.TempDir() with mode 0o755: "#!/bin/sh\necho '{\"type\":\"system\",\"subtype\":\"init\"}'\ncat\nexit 4\n"; p, err := Start(ctx, bin, nil, t.TempDir(), nil); when first <-p.Lines(); p.Write([]byte("{\"type\":\"user\"}\n")); next <-p.Lines(); p.Stop(); <-p.Exit(); then err nil; first line exactly {"type":"system","subtype":"init"}; the next line exactly {"type":"user"}; ExitStatus{Code: 4, Stderr: ""}; Lines() closed; p.PID() > 0
2. given the script "#!/bin/sh\necho oops >&2\nexit 2\n"; when Start, then <-p.Exit(); then ExitStatus{Code: 2, Stderr: "oops\n"}; a Write after it → ErrExited
3. given the script "#!/bin/sh\nsleep 30 &\necho started\nwait\n" (the background sleep holds stdout); when Start; first <-p.Lines(); p.Kill(); <-p.Exit() within 2 s; then the first line "started"; ExitStatus.Code -1 (the whole group is killed: a SIGKILL to sh alone leaves the sleep holding stdout, and Exit would come only after 30 s)
4. given Start(ctx, "/nonexistent/claude", nil, t.TempDir(), nil); Start(ctx, "sh", nil, "/nonexistent/dir", nil); when Start; then each (nil, an error beginning "claude: start ")
5. given the script "#!/bin/sh\nhead -c 70000 /dev/zero | tr '\\0' x; echo\necho short\n"; when Start; the two lines from Lines(); then the first line has length 70000 (longer than bufio's 64 KiB default), the second is "short"
6. given f := NewFake(); f.Emit([]byte(`{"type":"x"}`)); f.Write([]byte("a\n")); f.Write([]byte("b\n")); f.Finish(0); when read Lines() to the close; Written(); <-f.Exit(); f.Write([]byte("c\n")); f.Killed(); then one line {"type":"x"} then closed; Written [][]byte{"a\n", "b\n"}; ExitStatus{Code: 0}; ErrExited; false
7. given f := NewFake(); f.Kill(); when <-f.Exit(); Killed(); PID(); then ExitStatus{Code: -1}; true; 4242

## Function Project Create

Validate the request, run the create sequence through the runner, report every step; push once the token is there.

Behaviour: Declares in bootstrap/create.go: `type Spec struct { Name string; Language string; RepoURL string; ProjectsDir string; CredentialsFile string; MorphBin string }`, `type Report struct { Dir string `json:"dir"`; Steps []string `json:"steps"` }`, `func Create(ctx context.Context, r runner.Runner, s Spec) (Report, error)` and `func FirstPush(ctx context.Context, r runner.Runner, dir string) (bool, error)`. FirstPush (called when the GitHub token arrives): in dir, env []string{"GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0"}: git rev-parse --verify -q origin/main → Code 0 → (false, nil) (already pushed); else git push -q -u origin main → Code 0 → (true, nil); a non-zero Code → (false, "bootstrap: push failed (exit <code>): " + trimmed Stderr); a Run error → (false, "bootstrap: push: " + err.Error()). Create has eight steps (the push is FirstPush's). Checks first, in this order: Name matches ^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{0,39}$ else "bootstrap: bad project name \"<name>\""; Language is "typescript", "python" or "go" else "bootstrap: unknown language \"<l>\""; github.Parse(RepoURL) ok else its error; MorphBin not "" else "bootstrap: morph binary not configured"; dir := filepath.Join(ProjectsDir, Name) must not exist (os.Stat) else "bootstrap: directory exists: <dir>". Then the commands, each through r.Run with env []string{"GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0"}, in this order and with exactly these arguments: 1. in ProjectsDir: <MorphBin> init --root <dir> --name <Name> --language <Language>, and for Language "go" two
   more arguments --module <Name> (the Go template's module path); morph init refuses a non-empty target, a
   .git entry too, which is why git init comes after it
2. in dir: git init -q -b main 3. in dir: git config credential.helper "store --file=<CredentialsFile>" (one argument holding the space) 4. in dir: git config user.name morphd 5. in dir: git config user.email morphd@localhost 6. in dir: git remote add origin <RepoURL> 7. in dir: git add -A 8. in dir: git commit -q -m "morph init: <Name> (<Language>)" Report.Steps gets runner.Key(name, args...) of every command run. A Run error → (the report so far, "bootstrap: step <n>: " + err.Error()); a non-zero Code → (the report so far, "bootstrap: step <n> failed (exit <code>): " + strings.TrimSpace(Stderr)). Success → (Report{Dir: dir, Steps: the eight keys}, nil). The token is never an argument: the credentials file carries it.

Steps:
- uses: runner
- uses: github
- produces: Report

Examples (the tests must prove each one):
1. given f := &runner.Fake{} (every call Code 0); Create(ctx, f, Spec{Name: "demo", Language: "go", RepoURL: "https://github.com/o/demo", ProjectsDir: t.TempDir(), CredentialsFile: "/st/demo/git-credentials", MorphBin: "/usr/local/bin/morph"}); when Create; then error nil; Report.Dir == filepath.Join(ProjectsDir, "demo"); Steps exactly ["/usr/local/bin/morph init --root <dir> --name demo --language go --module demo", "git init -q -b main", "git config credential.helper store --file=/st/demo/git-credentials", "git config user.name morphd", "git config user.email morphd@localhost", "git remote add origin https://github.com/o/demo", "git add -A", "git commit -q -m morph init: demo (go)"]; f.Calls[0].Dir == ProjectsDir and f.Calls[1..7].Dir == dir; f.Calls[2].Args == ["config", "credential.helper", "store --file=/st/demo/git-credentials"]

## Component requirements / guardrails

Requirements:
- Claude Behind An Interface: The claude CLI is reached only through claude.Process (stdin lines in, stdout lines out, an exit status); the daemon's tests use claude.Fake fed with lines from tests/fixtures/stream/probe.jsonl, never a real claude.
- Bearer Token On Every Route: Every HTTP route but GET /healthz and the MCP endpoints requires Authorization: Bearer <MORPHD_TOKEN>; /mcp and /mcp/{project} require the same token; /mcp/{project}/session requires that project's current session token. morphd listens on 127.0.0.1 only; TLS and the public name are Caddy's.
- The Session Reports Only Itself: A VPS session can call phase_done, wait_operator and milestone only through its own endpoint /mcp/{project}/session with the token morphd minted for that spawn; the token changes on every spawn, so a past session or another project cannot report.

Guardrails:
- Injected Clock And Ids: No package but cmd/morphd reads the clock or a random source: time comes in as a `now` argument or an injected Now func() time.Time, ids from an injected NewID func() string; time.Now, math/rand and crypto/rand appear only in cmd/morphd. Timers are the daemon's Tick, driven by main's ticker.
- No Network In Tests: Tests never open a listener or dial: HTTP is tested with httptest.NewRecorder and httptest.NewRequest, Telegram and GitHub through an injected Do, the MCP server over in-memory transports; a test writes files only under t.TempDir(); no test runs claude or reaches github.com or api.telegram.org.
- No Shell Outside Runner: os/exec is imported only by package runner (git, morph) and package claude (the claude process); every other package runs commands through runner.Runner and tests script them with runner.Fake.
- Secrets Never Logged: The API token, the session tokens, the GitHub token and the Telegram token never appear in a response body, a log line, a milestone, an error text or the argv of a spawned process; secrets live in files of mode 0600 under the state directory; the git credentials reach git through a credential store file, never through a URL or an argument.
